title: Invertibility of the raw restricted evaluation map
statement: The evaluation morphism from derived Hom classes to zeroth derived sections of the restricted pullback, before the explicit shift identification, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03Q8 and Cohomology on Sites Tags 072W, 0BKV and 0D6F

proof.text: For K=F[0][p], use DerivedCategory.Plus.exists_injective_nonempty_iso to choose a bounded-below complex J of injective sheaves and an isomorphism QJ to K. Etale restriction to W preserves injectives (the abelian specialization injective_upperStar_obj_of_etale_addCommGrp); hence both J and its restriction are K-injective.

The homotopy-to-derived localization map on Hom(A[0],J) is bijective by Qh_map_bijective, and the bounded-below inclusion is fully faithful. The represented homotopy sections isomorphism supplies bijectivity on the source homotopy classes.

The explicit resolutionSectionsIso is invertible on the K-injective restriction. Every homotopy class lifts to a chain map; rawRestricted_resolution_evaluation identifies its composite with derived evaluation with the preceding homotopy sections isomorphism. Cancel the two bijections to obtain bijectivity of derived evaluation on QJ; the concrete category criterion gives IsIso.

For an additive T, postcomposition with an isomorphism e on Hom(A,-) commutes with evaluation since T.map(f followed by e)=T.map(e) followed by T.map(f). Both postcomposition and T.map(e) are invertible, so evaluation on QJ is invertible if and only if evaluation on K is. Apply the representative isomorphism.
